title: A made-up key with every shingle's text left off
story: As 4.2-cc8-made-up-key, but the client leaves the text off every one of A3's per-shingle values and removes nothing from A3's text. No shingle of A3 can then be compared with A1's or A2's, and A3's sketch reproduces under the client's key. The reviewer still sees all of A3's text.
edits: The transcript's user entry for each prompt, read by the log reader 0.7 to 4.5 s after the hook (via log, same turn_key and lengths), as a real Claude Code client records it.
A3's f is computed under a made-up key instead of K_feat. Its c is honest, and its content reveal removes nothing.
A3's shingle reveal gives each of its nine values under the made-up key, and none with its x.

CC5.basis: one device, whose scorer credits each slot to at most one project (SM 3.1)

CC6.basis: Stated, not recomputed: the live buckets are pkg/score over this device's events.jsonl, which the reveal holds in full, so the server's re-score is the same computation and every minute reproduces.

CC10.reason: no editor act in the submission

notes: Nothing was removed from A3, so every value must show its shingle, and the shown shingles must be exactly A3's (ledger-v1.md 10.8). A3's show none, so CC8 fails it (`shingles`). That rule is what keeps the cross-reveal rule working: without it, leaving x off is a cheaper way to hide a made-up key than removing words, as 4.2-cc8-removed-spans does, and it hides nothing from the reviewer.
ledger-v1.md 10.8 (WP-LG3, #12). Issue #15: CC8 is weaker than DESIGN 7.3 claims, and these cases follow the spec's stated limit
